source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
How it works now

\- USDC: Approve → auto-mint → success modal (only after mint).
\- ETH: Dynamic price calculation → sufficient buffer → successful swap.

The ETH price shown will fluctuate to match $15 USDC based on current market rates. The contract’s minETHForMint is 0.0055 ETH (~$16.50), so the frontend uses the higher of the dynamic price or this minimum.

Hard refresh your browser (Ctrl+Shift+R or Cmd+Shift+R) and try minting again.
Both USDC and ETH should work correctly.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Findings
Your ETH mint reverted (0x3af7…0855c on Base) because the on-chain swap router is set to 0x2626…e481, which isn’t the Uniswap V3 SwapRouter. The contract calls exactInputSingle there and it reverts, so every ETH mint will fail until the router is corrected on-chain.

USDC mint works;
\- token #1 exists and is owned by 0x3b55868Dd2ebA28f97b3dB55a4cB706a078154B5. Metadata and assets resolve:
\- Metadata: <https://api.projectrebuild.xyz/metadata/1>
\- Image: <https://api.projectrebuild.xyz/images/1.png>

execution.observed_behavior: Transaction inspection showed the ETH mint reverted because the contract pointed to a non-Uniswap swap router.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Q2: What about shortfall/excess?
Excess (get more than $15):
\- Refunded to the user in USDC (line 266-268)
\- Example: Swap gives $17 → User gets $2 USDC back

Shortfall (get less than $15):
\- Transaction reverts (line 263)
\- Example: Swap gives $14 → Entire transaction fails
User doesn't lose anything, just has to retry

execution.observed_behavior: Freelancer claims the current ETH swap refunds output above $15 in USDC and reverts without loss when output is below $15.
